title: Miso Glazed Udon with Chicken Gyoza
method: If using dried udon noodles, boil until al dente for 8–9 minutes, then drain and rinse under cold water; if using pre-cooked udon, heat according to package instructions, rinse under cold water, and set aside[cite: 23].
Whisk the miso paste, sugar, soy sauce, and rice vinegar together in a small bowl to make the glaze[cite: 23].
Heat 1 tsp neutral oil in a frying pan over low to medium heat, add the gyoza, and cook for 4 minutes[cite: 23].
Add 4 tbsp cold water to the pan, cover with a lid, and cook for another 4 minutes until the water evaporates[cite: 23]. Remove the gyoza from the pan and set aside[cite: 23].
Add another 1 tsp neutral oil to the pan, add the sugar snap peas, baby corn, and radishes, and stir-fry over medium heat for 2 minutes[cite: 23].
Pour in the miso glaze and simmer for 5 minutes until reduced to a thickened sauce consistency[cite: 23].
Add the noodles to the vegetables and sauce, tossing thoroughly to coat[cite: 23].
Divide the noodles and vegetables between two bowls, top with the cooked gyoza, pour over any remaining sauce from the pan, and garnish with fresh coriander[cite: 23].
